SDF-based voxel rendering is a simpler, non-differentiable approach demonstrated in holographic_fractals [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a voxel rendering approach using Signed Distance Functions (SDF). The code snippets show iterating through a 3D volume, evaluating an SDF (or equivalent geometric condition) at each voxel center, and drawing the voxel if the condition is met (SDF <= 0). This matches the 'SDF-based voxel rendering' part of the claim. The claim describes this as 'simpler' and 'non-differentiable'. The evidence shows a brute-force iteration over a grid with simple geometric checks (length comparisons), which is computationally simpler than ray-marching or differentiable rendering techniques, and the operations (comparisons, lengths) are not differentiable in the context of gradient-based optimization (they are discrete/step functions). The reference to 'holographic_fractals [S2, unofficial]' aligns with the provided source [S2] which appears to be an unofficial or example implementation (indicated by the filename `full_volume_threaded.c` and the nature of the code).
